newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Real Software price due later on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Real Software price due later on Tuesday.

text.p: A price range for shares in Belgian information technology (IT) services firm Real Software, to be listed on the Brussels bourse in early June, will be set later on Tuesday, lead manager KB Securities said.
The spread between the lower and the higher price would amount to 12 to 13 percent. It was not immediately clear when the final issue price would be set.
The company, currently management-owned, is offering about 450,000 existing shares, or 38 percent of its capital, to the public in the deal co-lead by Generale Bank and Bank Degroof.
The offering is conditional upon approval from the Bank and Finance Commission, the market watchdog.
Financial analyst Johan Pede at KB Securities said it was hard to give comparable price/earnings ratios for the sector. "The range is very wide...15 to 40 percent."
For example, New York listed U.S. Electronic Data Systems, active in the same sector, has a P/E of about 39.
Pede had no comment on Belgian newspaper reports that the operation could be worth 700 million Belgian francs to the company.
Pede said Real Software had known uninterrupted growth in profit and sales since its foundation in 1986.
The software development and implementation company has 400 employees, annual turnover of some 1.2 billion francs, of which one third is realised abroad, and pre-tax profit of 180 million francs.
Pede put operational (Earnings before Interest and Tax, EBIT) margins at 10 to 20 percent and foresaw market growth of 10 to 20 percent in the 1997-2000 period.
He said the risks for a stock such as Real Software were limited. "The company has preferential partnerships with numerous large companies."

Prospects were good with a view to a need for IT services in the run-up to the year 2000, when changes in dates could cause disruptions to hard- and software and databases, and the launch of Europe's single currency, the euro, he said.

Real Software is the second Belgian IT firm to come to the market in the first half of 1997. Systemat NV, founded in 1984, offers hardware, configuration, assembly, installation, training and support services.
Systemat stock was down eight francs at 1,300 at 0940 GMT on Tuesday on a firmer Brussels bourse.
A study by Vermeulen Raemdonck, the brokerage of bank BBL which is lead-managing the issue, put Systemat's estimated 1997 P/E at 14.9 and 11.2 for 1998.
